title: Jimmy Blanton, Lee and Lester's band at the Capri, and Duke's offer
summary: Callender recalls friendship with Blanton and Billy Strayhorn, and turning down Elmer Fain's offer of a place with Duke so he could keep writing and playing tuba.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Blanton and I became friends. As a matter of fact, when Blanton got sick... Well, we were good friends. I was with him the day before he died. Lee Young and I and Billy Strayhorn; you know, we used to hang out together. At that time, I was working with Lee in Lester's band... I'm jumping around, but that's the way it comes.
I was working with Lee in Lester Young's band at the Capri...
This is Billy Berg's club, right?

Billy Berg's Capri. And Elmer Fain said, 'Hey, do you want to go with Duke?' And I said, 'Wow, that's wonderful, but I really would rather stay here and learn more about music.' Because I knew if I went with Duke, I'd never get to play my tuba and I'd never get to write. And I was writing for Lee and Lester's band, and I also wrote for a lot of bands... I used to write for shows around town.
But before that, let me to 19...
